title: Merge and rebase on the same fork
purpose: See how merge and rebase join the same two diverged branches and why the two histories differ.
sequence_reason: Each command moves pointers and creates commits in a fixed order, and the result of each step depends on the step before.
summary: Commits C1 and C2 sit on main. The branch feature adds C3 and main adds C4, both with the parent C2. On main, git merge feature records a merge commit C5 with the two parents C4 and C3. On feature, git rebase main replays C3 on top of C4 as a new commit C3', so history is a straight line. Both give the same final files, so rebase only commits that exist only in your repository.
explanation: A branch is a movable pointer to a commit. Merge adds a commit with two parents and rewrites nothing; rebase copies your commits as new commits on top of the other branch (Pro Git 3.1, 3.2, 3.6).

learning_check.question: After git rebase main on feature, is C3 still the tip of feature?
learning_check.answer: No. Rebase creates a new commit C3' with the parent C4, and feature now points to C3'. The old C3 is no longer on the branch.

scenes.heading: Commits, branches and HEAD
scenes.narration: Each commit stores a snapshot and a link to its parent. A branch is a movable pointer, and HEAD names your current branch.

items: Commit: a snapshot plus a parent link
Branch: a pointer to one commit
HEAD: the branch you are on
New commit: your branch moves forward

scenes.heading: One history forks into two
scenes.narration: Now the history forks into two lines. Feature adds C3, main adds C4, and both commits have the parent C2.

left.label: feature
items: C3, parent C2
feature points to C3

right.label: main
items: C4, parent C2
main points to C4

visual.verdict: C2 is the common ancestor of both tips.

scenes.heading: git merge feature, on main
scenes.narration: On main, git merge feature combines C4, C3 and their common ancestor C2. Git records C5, a merge commit with two parents.

items: Find the common ancestor C2
Three-way merge of C4 and C3
Record merge commit C5 with two parents
main moves to C5, feature stays at C3

scenes.heading: git rebase main, on feature
scenes.narration: On feature, git rebase main replays the change of C3 on top of C4 as a new commit, C3'. History becomes a straight line.

items: Save the change that C3 made
Reset feature to C4, the tip of main
Apply the change as new commit C3'
History is one straight line

scenes.heading: Same files, different history
scenes.narration: Both commands give the same final files, but rebase rewrites commits. Never rebase commits that exist outside your repository.

left.label: Merge
items: Keeps both lines of work
Adds a commit with two parents
Rewrites no commits

right.label: Rebase
items: One straight line
Creates new commits
Safe for local commits only

visual.verdict: Do not rebase commits that exist outside your repository.
